editions.text:
The station recorded 26 species and 323 feeder visits, a busier day than the previous week's average of 20 species and 303.6 visits. Core regulars held strong, with Tufted Titmouse, Carolina Wren, and Eastern Towhee maintaining consistent presence throughout the day. White-eyed Vireo returned to the audio logs after a 12-day absence, while Rose-breasted Grosbeak, Cedar Waxwing, and Brown-headed Cowbird were absent.

Visual activity was dominated by Tufted Titmouse, which accounted for 157 of the total visits, followed by Carolina Chickadee and White-breasted Nuthatch. Northern Cardinal marked both the first visual record at 11 minutes before sunrise and the last at 5 minutes after sunset. The installed woodpecker brick on the cage feeder coincides with the day's single Pileated Woodpecker visit, though no other species changes align with recent station modifications.

The second microphone added in September continues to capture a wider range of calls, including a single Eastern Screech-Owl detection in the early hours. The single Northern Flicker visit remained probable.
